subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Where should the conditional be placed so that the project is always checking if the moving sprite has overlapped with the player sprite?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ When should the project check to see if the player sprite has overlapped with the moving sprite?


Solution: 

The entire if conditional should be moved inside the curly brackets of the forever loop.

﻿
steps.instructions:
When the moving sprite overlaps with the player sprite, nothing happens!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the project ends in a loss and an effect runs once the moving sprite overlaps the player sprite.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you check the syntax of the forever loop code to make sure that each set of parentheses and curly brackets has an opening and closing pair?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Based on the error message, what symbol should be placed at the end of the forever loop so that the code is able to run?


Solution: 

A closing parenthesis ) should be added to the end of the block statement of the forever loop (to the right of the closing curly bracket }).
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice that the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 58: ) was expected.



Fix the bugs in the code so that when the project is run, it continuously checks to see if the player sprite is overlapping the moving sprite.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about conditionals and nested block statements. Nested block statements are created when code inside of curly brackets is placed inside of another chunk of code in curly brackets, such as placing a conditional inside of a forever loop. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Curly Brackets All the Way Down
badges.description: Use nested block statements to place one block statement inside another in JavaScript.

badges.title: If at First You Don’t Succeed
badges.description: Use  “if” and “if / else” statements in JavaScript.

badges.title: ...or Else
badges.description: Use an “else if” statement in JavaScript.

badges.title: Until the End of Time
badges.description: Use a forever loop in JavaScript.

badges.title: Hey I’m Walking Here
badges.description: Use the overlapsWith function to see if two sprites are overlapping.

badges.title: Gaming the System
badges.description: Use the setGameOverEffect and gameOver functions to customize game over screens.

badges.title: The Final Countdown
badges.description: Use the info.onCountdownEnd function to run code when the countdown reaches zero.

badges.title: Playing the Odds
badges.description: Use the Math.percentChance function inside an if statement to add randomness to a project.

badges.title: A Flair for the Dramatic
badges.description: Add a custom sprite effect to a sprite.

badges.title: Let’s Try That Again
badges.description: Use the game.reset function to restart a project.
